inevitable_need: Before any agent touches a service, it automatically gets the incidents, postmortem findings and 'never do X here' constraints for the exact files and services it is about to change, and it stops for a human when the change hits something that has burned us before.
why_inevitable: Agents are already writing a growing share of our PRs and they have zero memory of why things broke last time, so it's only a matter of time before one ships a repeat of an incident we already paid for. Once that happens I either build this myself or buy it, because I'm not going back to humans reviewing every agent diff by hand.
must_have: Pulls from our actual incident history and postmortems and maps them to code paths and services, with a link to the source for every warning
Plugs straight into Claude Code and Cursor (MCP or hook) with no change to how engineers run agents, and adds seconds, not minutes
Low noise: it says nothing or 'I don't know' rather than padding every briefing with generic Slack chatter
deal_breakers: Requires sending our incident history and repo access to an unproven third-party cloud with no self-host option
Floods agents and reviewers with false-positive warnings so people learn to ignore it
Needs a dedicated person to curate or tag knowledge by hand to stay useful
expected_provider: Honestly, probably the agent makers themselves (Anthropic, Cursor) or GitHub will bolt on some version of repo memory, and if that's not good enough my platform engineer will hack a version together on our postmortems. A startup wins only if it's clearly better on incident recall and gets there before those two do; I don't expect Glean or Notion to do this well because they index docs, not code paths.
memoryworks_would_need: The agent-briefing piece is exactly what I described, but it has to prove itself on our own repo by catching a real repeat before it ships, with a low false-positive rate. After that I'd pay roughly $500-600 a month flat for a hosted version only if it's out of early preview with a clear security story (SOC 2 or equivalent, scoped read-only repo access), otherwise I stay on the free self-hosted version.
